_meta.description: Prescription-access tiers for amphetamine-class ADHD stimulants (amphetamine, dexamphetamine, lisdexamfetamine/Vyvanse) vs. methylphenidate-class vs. non-stimulant-only. NOT legal or medical advice. Confidence/evidence fields indicate how well-sourced each entry is — treat 'low' confidence entries as needing further verification before relying on them.

tiers.1: At least one amphetamine-class ADHD stimulant (dexamphetamine and/or lisdexamfetamine) is approved and routinely prescribable under controlled-substance regulations. Brand availability (e.g. Adderall specifically) does not matter for this tier.
tiers.2: Amphetamine-class ADHD stimulants are not approved or generally unavailable; methylphenidate (Ritalin/Concerta) is available, possibly with heavy restrictions on quantity/duration.
tiers.3: Amphetamine-class unavailable AND methylphenidate-class also unavailable/unapproved; only non-stimulant options (atomoxetine, clonidine, guanfacine, etc.)
tiers.4: Effectively no approved ADHD pharmacological treatment infrastructure / unclear or unregulated
tiers.unknown: Not yet researched, or researched but evidence only covers travel/import rules rather than domestic prescribing — insufficient to assign a tier

field_definitions.confidence: high | medium | low — how well the evidence supports this specific tier assignment
field_definitions.evidence: government (regulator/formulary/law) | peer_review (published study) | clinical (named practitioner/clinic) | community (advocacy org, forum, travel blog) | mixed
field_definitions.approved: booleans for whether each drug class is approved/routinely prescribable domestically; null = not established
field_definitions.last_verified: year-month this entry's sources were checked

US.notes: Schedule II controlled substance; Adderall, dexamphetamine, and Vyvanse all routinely prescribable.

CA.notes: General knowledge, not independently re-verified against Health Canada this session; regulatory pattern closely mirrors the US.

GB.notes: Elvanse (lisdexamfetamine) and dexamfetamine both licensed and prescribable. Adderall brand specifically is not marketed there, which does not affect this tier.

AU.notes: Schedule 8 controlled drug; dexamphetamine and lisdexamfetamine both prescribable under strict specialist-authority rules. Not independently re-verified against TGA this session.

NZ.notes: Assumed similar to Australia's framework; not independently checked.

DE.notes: Methylphenidate first-line; dexamfetamine and lisdexamfetamine both approved as second-line/adult options.

sources: ANSM (French National Agency for Medicines and Health Products Safety) - 2025/2026 Authorizations
FR.notes: Historically Tier 2/3 with restrictive methylphenidate-only policies, France moved to Tier 1 following the 2025/2026 approval of XURTA (lisdexamfetamine) with full marketing authorization, granting access to amphetamine-based treatment.

sources: DARWIN EU / Lancet Regional Health-Europe study
NL.notes: Dexamfetamine and lisdexamfetamine both in active clinical use; adult prescribing is often off-label but real and tracked in national health-record studies.

SE.notes: Sweden has a highly progressive ADHD treatment model. Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) is approved for both children and adults. Dexamphetamine (Attentin) is available. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are standard.

sources: ADHD-Europe AISBL 2021 Survey on Diagnosis and Treatment
European Medicines Agency (EMA) - DARWIN EU ADHD Medication Utilisation
IT.notes: Italy remains highly restricted. Amphetamine-based medications are strictly prohibited. Methylphenidate (Ritalin/Equasym) and atomoxetine are the only approved treatments, and adult prescription is notoriously difficult, with frequent national stock shortages reported.

AT.notes: Elvanse, compounded amphetamine sulfate, and dexamfetamine (Philla) all prescribable via narcotic prescription. Source is a patient advocacy org, not the Austrian regulator directly, though it cites specific legal prescribing mechanisms.

BE.notes: Dexamfetamine approved and used, though dispensing is restricted to hospital pharmacies rather than all retail pharmacies.

DK.notes: Denmark was one of the first adopters in the European Decentralised Procedure for lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse/Aduvanz). Dexamphetamine (Attentin) is also approved for cases where lisdexamfetamine is insufficient.

NO.notes: Norway fully covers ADHD medications. Lisdexamfetamine is marketed as Aduvanz/Elvanse and dexamphetamine (Attentin) is available. Like Sweden and Denmark, it provides comprehensive access to both stimulant classes.

FI.notes: Finland participated in the UK-led decentralized procedure for lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) and maintains standard Nordic availability. Dexamphetamine (Attentin) is also registered.

CH.notes: Lisdexamfetamine and dexmethylphenidate (Focalin) both available; included in an EU-wide prescription-database study.

sources: Takeda/Shire Pharmaceuticals: Elvanse/Tyvense European Decentralised Procedure Authorisation
IE.notes: Ireland offers broad access. Lisdexamfetamine is marketed under the brand name Tyvense (rather than Elvanse). Methylphenidate and Atomoxetine are standard first and second-line treatments.

sources: Takeda/Shire Pharmaceuticals: Elvanse European Decentralised Procedure Authorisation
AEMPS (Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices) CIMA database
ES.notes: Spain offers full access to standard European ADHD medications. Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) was approved via the UK MHRA European Decentralised Procedure. Methylphenidate (Concerta, Rubifen) is widely prescribed as a first-line treatment.

sources: PMC10932761 (Practical clinical guidelines and pharmacological treatment for ADHD in Asia, 2023)
Japanese Guidelines for Diagnosis and Treatment of ADHD, 5th Edition (2022)
JP.notes: Japan approves OROS-methylphenidate, lisdexamfetamine (LDX), atomoxetine, and guanfacine extended release for ADHD. LDX is available as third-line treatment. Strict controlled-substance regulations limit prescribing but do not prohibit amphetamine-class medications.

KR.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS). Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are approved under a heavy digital tracking network. All amphetamine variants are illegal under the Narcotics Control Act.
KR.notes: MFDS utilizes an AI-driven Narcotics Information Management System to crack down on over-prescribing. Amphetamines are strictly banned for import.

sources: PMC8863856 (Utilization of Drugs for ADHD Among Young Patients in China, 2010-2019)
PMC10932761 (Practical clinical guidelines and pharmacological treatment for ADHD in Asia)
CN.notes: Only methylphenidate and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in China. Methylphenidate is the most frequently prescribed medication, with atomoxetine as second-line. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved.

HK.notes: Methylphenidate (Ritalin, Ritalin LA, Concerta) is the standard prescribed treatment. Amphetamine is classified as a dangerous drug alongside methamphetamine under Hong Kong law; Adderall specifically is not approved for domestic use.

IN.notes: Methylphenidate available; amphetamine-class prescribing inconsistent across states. Not independently re-verified against Indian regulatory sources this session.

NP.notes: Nepal's official banned-drug list explicitly bans amphetamine and its combinations. The public DDA registry evidence reviewed here supports atomoxetine registration, but not methylphenidate or amphetamine-class stimulant approval.

sources: INFARMED (National Authority of Medicines and Health Products, Portugal)
PT.notes: Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) and Methylphenidate (Concerta, Ritalin) are approved but strictly classified as controlled psychotropics. Dexamfetamine is not separately authorized but lisdexamfetamine is actively prescribed.

sources: SÚKL (State Institute for Drug Control, Czech Republic)
EMA Elvanse Patient Information Leaflet Data
CZ.notes: Czechia approves lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) alongside standard methylphenidate and atomoxetine formulations, bringing them into Tier 1 access for Central Europe.

sources: The exponential increase in the number of prescriptions for ADHD medication between 2012 and 2022 in Poland in patients aged 5–59 years: a pharmacoepidemiological study (ResearchGate)
PL.notes: Methylphenidate (e.g., Medikinet) is the most prescribed ADHD medication. Atomoxetine is also approved and increasingly used. There are no approved amphetamine-class stimulants available for ADHD in Poland.

sources: RELEXXII Methylphenidate HCl Extended-Release Tablets for ADHD
GR.notes: Methylphenidate (e.g., Ritalin, Relexxii, Concerta) is the approved first-line stimulant for ADHD in Greece. Amphetamine-class medications like lisdexamfetamine are not locally approved; patients entering Greece with these prescriptions require special Schengen certificates.

sources: ADHD diagnoses more than triple in 5 years - news | ERR
EE.notes: Methylphenidate (Medikinet) is the primary subsidized ADHD stimulant in Estonia, with recent expansions in adult subsidies. Amphetamine-class medications are not generally approved or prescribable locally.

sources: Global Trends in ADHD Medication Use: Multiple Contexts and Rising Concerns—A Narrative Review (PMC)
IS.notes: Icelandic Medicines Registry data and multinational reviews confirm the utilization and approval of methylphenidate, dexamphetamine, lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse), and atomoxetine.

sources: Ref: A.19 Methylphenidate – attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (Romanian Society of Child and Adolescent Neurology and Psychiatry)
RO.notes: Methylphenidate (specifically Concerta) is authorized and strictly classified as a high-risk drug in Romania, acting as the standard stimulant option in their ADHD treatment protocol. No amphetamines are approved.

CL.notes: Methylphenidate and Lisdexamfetamine are clinically available for ADHD treatment under strict 'receta cheque' (check prescription) requirements. Atomoxetine is approved, though it has previously faced market supply adjustments. Amphetamine-based stimulants like Adderall (mixed salts) or pure dexamphetamine are not typically registered for clinical use in Chile.

sources: Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association
PK.notes: Methylphenidate (e.g., Ritalin) is widely available and used clinically for ADHD. Atomoxetine is also available (e.g., brand name Attenttra). Amphetamine-based stimulants like Lisdexamfetamine or mixed amphetamine salts are not standardly available through official clinical channels in Pakistan.

sources: Directorate General of Drug Administration (DGDA) Bangladesh
BD.notes: Methylphenidate is registered and available under brands like Alaradate and Methyphen. Atomoxetine is also widely available through major local manufacturers such as Square, Incepta, and UniMed UniHealth. Amphetamine-based stimulants like lisdexamfetamine are generally not registered for clinical use.

sources: PMC10932761 (Practical clinical guidelines and pharmacological treatment for ADHD in Asia, 2023)
MY.notes: Malaysia's MOH Medicines Formulary only approves methylphenidate and atomoxetine for ADHD. Lisdexamfetamine is not listed and cannot be filled locally. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved.

SG.notes: Methylphenidate (Ritalin, Concerta, Medikinet) is the most widely prescribed first-line option. Health authorities expanded options by officially making Vyvanse (lisdexamfetamine) available for prescription.

TW.evidence: Regulated by the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA). Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are approved and covered under National Health Insurance. Amphetamine derivatives are completely banned.
TW.notes: Methylphenidate is managed as a Class 3 Controlled Drug. Bringing unapproved amphetamines into the country is treated as a narcotics offense.

TH.notes: Methylphenidate is fully approved as a Schedule II psychotropic substance. Both short-acting (Ritalin) and long-acting (Ritalin LA, Concerta) formulations are available. Lisdexamfetamine is classified as a Category 1 narcotic with no recognized medical use - it is illegal to possess, import, or prescribe. Travelers may carry a maximum 30-day supply of methylphenidate with a valid medical certificate in English. No prior Thai FDA permit is required for methylphenidate travelers.

PH.notes: Methylphenidate is the primary approved stimulant for ADHD. Amphetamine-based stimulants are not commonly registered or approved for ADHD treatment in the Philippines.

VN.notes: Methylphenidate is approved for limited use in psychiatric settings. Amphetamines are strictly controlled and not available for ADHD.

ID.notes: Methylphenidate is clinically approved and available with a local prescription, but it is a strictly controlled psychotropic. Amphetamine-based stimulants are generally classified as Category I narcotics and are banned. Personal import of psychotropics by foreigners is subject to extreme regulatory scrutiny and requires specific documentation; local psychiatric assessment is mandatory for ongoing supply.

KH.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health. Amphetamines are strictly prohibited for therapeutic use. Methylphenidate is heavily restricted under psychotropic control laws and rarely available outside specialized international clinics.
KH.notes: Extremely limited domestic supply chain. Generally inaccessible in commercial public retail pharmacies.

LA.notes: Methylphenidate is permitted for clinical use but is extremely limited in availability, often requiring procurement through specialty channels or private hospitals in Vientiane. Other ADHD medications such as lisdexamfetamine or atomoxetine are not formally registered or widely accessible.

BN.notes: Methylphenidate is available in the public health system. Amphetamines are generally not part of the standard ADHD formulary.

TL.notes: There is no formal ADHD treatment infrastructure or registered pharmacological ADHD management in Timor-Leste.

SA.notes: Methylphenidate (Concerta, Ritalin) and Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) are SFDA-approved for ADHD. Atomoxetine (Strattera) is also approved and available. Access to stimulants requires a local prescription and is strictly regulated; travelers must obtain electronic clearance via the SFDA Controlled Drug System before arrival.

AE.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP). Methylphenidate and lisdexamfetamine are registered but highly controlled (Controlled Drug Class A). Mixed amphetamine salts are prohibited. Online e-import permit mandatory for travel.
AE.notes: Travelers must apply for a permit via the MOHAP portal prior to arrival. Strict psychotropic scheduling rules apply.

ZA.notes: Methylphenidate widely used; amphetamine-class prescribing more limited. Not independently re-verified this session.

BR.notes: Lisdexamfetamine (Venvanse) and methylphenidate both prescribable under ANVISA controlled-substance rules.

MX.notes: Vyvanse (lisdexamfetamine) is a COFEPRIS-registered Grupo II psychotropic under Mexico's health law - the existence of official government counterfeit alerts confirms it's a genuine registered product, not just theoretically approved. Adderall has no legal equivalent in Mexico. Supply caveat: Takeda withdrew Vyvanse from the Mexican market in 2021 and only relaunched it in February 2026, so 'legal' did not mean 'available' for several years - worth keeping availability and real-world supply as separate questions if this matters for your use case.

NG.evidence: Regulated by NAFDAC. Methylphenidate is officially approved as a controlled narcotic substance. Amphetamine formulations are not registered on the current standard national formulary.
NG.notes: Available almost exclusively through tertiary teaching hospitals or psychiatric institutions rather than open commercial pharmacy retail lines.

ET.evidence: Regulated by the Ethiopian Food and Drug Authority (EFDA). Methylphenidate is heavily bottlenecked and designated for institutional use only. Amphetamines are legally categorized as dangerous substances of abuse.
ET.notes: No routine commercial therapeutic pipelines exist for central nervous system stimulants. High import barriers apply.

CD.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament (DPM). Lack of structured national supply framework or commercial registrations for stimulants. Subject to stringent anti-narcotic enforcement laws.
CD.notes: ADHD diagnostics and therapeutics are practically absent from the public healthcare system. Unauthorized possession carries heavy penalties.

TZ.notes: Methylphenidate appears available; amphetamine-class approval not confirmed.

KE.evidence: Regulated by the Pharmacy and Poisons Board (PPB). Methylphenidate is registered under Schedule 1/Part I Poison laws. Amphetamines are completely unapproved and unregistered.
KE.notes: Stimulants require specialized hardcopy narcotic prescription sheets. Accessible mostly via private tier-one hospitals in major cities.

MM.notes: Methylphenidate is the primary stimulant used in clinical settings for ADHD, but availability is highly centralized in major urban medical centers and often subject to significant supply chain interruptions. Non-stimulants like atomoxetine and alternatives like lisdexamfetamine are generally unavailable through standard pharmacies.

CO.evidence: Regulated by INVIMA. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are fully approved. Lisdexamfetamine is registered but subject to extreme psychotropic control mechanisms and volatile localized supply chains.
CO.notes: Requires a special control prescription (recetario oficial de control) issued strictly by licensed specialists.

UG.evidence: Regulated by the National Drug Authority (NDA). Methylphenidate is categorized as a Class A controlled narcotic substance. Amphetamine variants are unregistered and legally unavailable.
UG.notes: Dispensing is limited to specialized, tracked psychiatric institutional centers such as Butabika Hospital.

SD.notes: Methylphenidate appears available; amphetamine-class approval not confirmed.

sources: Federal Law on Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances
RU.notes: Methylphenidate (Ritalin, Concerta) and atomoxetine (Strattera) are approved for ADHD in Russia. Amphetamine-class stimulants are strictly controlled under the Narcotic Drugs Act and not routinely approved for ADHD treatment.

sources: Turkish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency (TITCK)
TR.notes: Methylphenidate, lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse), and atomoxetine are approved for ADHD in Turkey. Lisdexamfetamine was approved via the European Decentralised Procedure. Amphetamine and mixed amphetamine salts are not approved.

sources: ANMAT (Administracion Nacional de Medicamentos, Alimentos y Tecnologia Medica)
AR.notes: Argentina has a relatively permissive ADHD medication framework. Methylphenidate, dexamphetamine, lisdexamfetamine, mixed amphetamine salts, and atomoxetine are all available under controlled-substance regulations.

sources: Croatian Agency for Medicinal Products and Medical Devices (HALMED)
HR.notes: Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) is approved in Croatia via the European Decentralised Procedure. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are standard treatments.

sources: National Institute of Pharmacy and Nutrition (OGYÉI) Hungary
HU.notes: Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) is approved in Hungary via the European Decentralised Procedure. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are standard treatments.

SK.notes: Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) is approved in Slovakia via the European Decentralised Procedure. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are standard treatments.

LV.notes: Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) is approved in Latvia via the European Decentralised Procedure. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are standard treatments.

CY.notes: Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse) is approved in Cyprus via the European Decentralised Procedure. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are standard treatments.

EG.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in Egypt. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not routinely approved or available.

LK.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are reported to be available in Sri Lanka. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved. Limited regulatory information available.

QA.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in Qatar. Amphetamine-class stimulants are strictly controlled under narcotics regulations.

sources: Kuwait Pharmacy and Drug Control Authority
KW.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in Kuwait. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved.

LB.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are reported to be available in Lebanon. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved.

IQ.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are reported to be available in Iraq. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved. Limited regulatory information available.

IR.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in Iran. Amphetamine-class stimulants are strictly controlled under narcotics regulations.

UA.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in Ukraine. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved.

CR.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in Costa Rica. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved.

UY.notes: Methylphenidate, dexamphetamine, lisdexamfetamine, and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in Uruguay. Amphetamine-class stimulants are available under controlled-substance regulations.

TT.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are reported to be available in Trinidad and Tobago. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved. Limited regulatory information available.

DZ.evidence: Regulated by the Ministère de la Santé and the National National Agency for Pharmaceutical Products (ANPP). Methylphenidate is approved but strictly classified as a Table A psychotropic substance. Amphetamines are not registered for therapeutic use.
DZ.notes: Prescriptions require specialized triplicate control forms issued exclusively by hospital psychiatrists. Strict quantity limits apply at customs.

BJ.evidence: Regulated by the Agence Béninoise de Régulation Pharmaceutique (ABRP). Follows rigid regional West African UEMOA narcotic guidelines. Methylphenidate is authorized under strict import quotas; amphetamines are completely unregistered.
BJ.notes: Sourcing is highly irregular and confined to select institutional pharmacies in Cotonou. Requires validated doctor authorization.

BF.evidence: Regulated by the Agence Nationale de Régulation Pharmaceutique (ANRP). Amphetamines are illegal for clinical medical use. Methylphenidate is legally classified under scheduled psychotropics but is rarely stocked in national distribution cycles.
BF.notes: Severe localized availability bottlenecks. Medical supplies face structural logistical disruptions outside major metropolitan centers.

BI.evidence: Regulated by the Autorité de Régulation des Médicaments et des Aliments (ABREMA). No registered commercial licenses exist for amphetamine salts, dexamphetamine, or lisdexamfetamine. Methylphenidate is theoretically classified as a controlled narcotic but lacks consistent formal import lines.
BI.notes: ADHD treatments are severely limited within the public system. Travelers face extreme scrutiny without legalized psychiatric documentation.

CF.evidence: Regulated by the Ministère de la Santé et de la Population. Central nervous system stimulants lack structured regulatory registry logs or standard tracking systems. Unauthorized amphetamines or methylphenidate are subject to immediate seizure.
CF.notes: Public healthcare infrastructure prioritizing endemic diseases; specialized neuropsychiatric medications are completely absent from normal commercial trade.

TD.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament. Commercial or therapeutic registration of amphetamine formulations is absent. Methylphenidate is heavily controlled and isolated strictly to military or direct ministry exceptions.
TD.notes: Strict border drug interdiction protocols are in effect. Possession without heavy official authorization is legally risky.

CG.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament (DPM) of the Republic of the Congo. Methylphenidate is approved strictly under custom import authorizations. Amphetamines are not registered for therapeutic distribution.
CG.notes: Highly scarce. Medications can generally only be sourced through highly specialized channels in Brazzaville or Pointe-Noire.

DJ.evidence: Regulated by the Ministère de la Santé. Methylphenidate is managed under tight narcotic scheduling rules matching historical French health frameworks. Amphetamines are not approved or imported.
DJ.notes: Stocks are rare and limited to specialized military or international private clinics in the capital city.

GQ.evidence: Regulated by the Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social. There is no public record of standard registrations for amphetamine products or atomoxetine. Methylphenidate is restricted under specific psychotropic monitoring laws.
GQ.notes: Relying on imported items with volatile stock rates. All personal quantities must be accompanied by certified Spanish translations of prescriptions.

ER.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health. Central nervous system stimulants (methylphenidate and amphetamines) are not listed on the national core formulary of essential medicines. Strictly restricted to avoid diversion.
ER.notes: Therapeutic infrastructure for neurodevelopmental care is severely underdeveloped. Bringing stimulants across checkpoints requires specialized state clearance.

SZ.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health. Closely follows South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) trends. Methylphenidate is registered as a Schedule 5/6 controlled substance. Amphetamines are not registered.
SZ.notes: Requires verified cross-border diagnostic forms. Sourced almost entirely from regional tertiary private medical networks.

GA.evidence: Regulated by the Agence du Médicament du Gabon (AMED). Methylphenidate is integrated into high-level psychotropic classifications. Amphetamine-based formulations are completely unregistered.
GA.notes: Requires mandatory validated documentation from a licensed psychiatric specialist to clear national custom entry ports.

GM.evidence: Regulated by the Medicines Control Agency (MCA) Gambia. Amphetamines are strictly unapproved. Methylphenidate is subject to high-level narcotic restrictions and is not routinely stocked in general public healthcare routes.
GM.notes: Requires direct individual clinical exception permits from the MCA for any legitimate personal transit imports.

GN.evidence: Regulated by the Direction Nationale de la Pharmacie et du Médicament (DNPM). Amphetamine formulations remain unregistered. Methylphenidate availability is unstable and strictly ring-fenced to specialized psychiatric programs.
GN.notes: High volumes of counterfeit products in parallel informal networks mean strict state checks are applied to genuine controlled prescriptions.

GW.evidence: Regulated by the Direcção-Geral da Farmácia. Formal public tracking or registration entries do not exist for modern ADHD stimulants. Amphetamines are strictly unapproved.
GW.notes: Severe systemic instability has limited access to psychiatric pharmaceuticals. Sourcing via public commercial channels is functionally non-existent.

LS.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health. Interlinked tightly with South African pharmaceutical regulatory listings. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are approved under controlled psychotropic classifications. Amphetamines are unregistered.
LS.notes: Dispensed almost exclusively at select specialized clinical points in Maseru. Border entry checks demand highly formalized medical tracking notes.

LR.evidence: Regulated by the Liberia Medicines and Health Products Regulatory Authority (LMHRA). Amphetamines are unlisted and prohibited. Methylphenidate is managed under dangerous psychotropic schedules with no stable retail tracking supply chain.
LR.notes: Access to pediatric or adult ADHD psychopharmacology is extremely constrained outside specialized international medical deployments.

MW.evidence: Regulated by the Pharmacy and Medicines Regulatory Authority (PMRA). Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are listed under strict narcotic and psychotropic schedules. Amphetamine configurations are not registered on the national database.
MW.notes: Requires custom certified pink prescription templates from psychiatric hospitals. Unauthorized imports are severely penalized under anti-diversion acts.

ML.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament (DPM). Amphetamines are completely prohibited for therapeutic distribution. Methylphenidate is theoretically registered under restricted psychotropic guidelines.
ML.notes: Sourcing challenges are extreme. Supplies are rarely tracked outside specific institutional channels in Bamako.

MR.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et du Laboratoire. Psychotropic controls are exceptionally high to block illicit transit pipelines. Amphetamines are banned. Methylphenidate is heavily restricted and unavailable commercially.
MR.notes: Unverified stimulant medications found at security points carry a high risk of strict legal or border interdiction without exhaustive ministerial paperwork.

MA.evidence: Regulated by the Direction du Médicament et de la Pharmacie (DMP). Methylphenidate is fully approved and strictly cataloged under the 'Tableau A' narcotic designation. Atomoxetine is approved. Amphetamines are strictly unapproved.
MA.notes: Prescription renewals are strictly capped at limited-day cycles (typically 28 days) and require rigorous oversight from licensed neurologists or psychiatrists.

NE.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et de la Médecine Traditionnelle. Therapeutic amphetamines are completely illegal. Methylphenidate is structurally controlled under psychotropic schedules with no routine domestic commercial distribution pipeline.
NE.notes: Severe systemic shortages disrupt mental health therapeutics. Carrying stimulants across internal security checkpoints is heavily restricted.

RW.evidence: Regulated by the Rwanda Food and Drugs Authority (Rwanda FDA). Achieved WHO Maturity Level 3. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are officially registered on the national list of approved human medicines. Amphetamines are not registered.
RW.notes: Strictly monitored as a controlled psychotropic substance. Dispensing requires validated tracking records from regional referral medical complexes.

SL.evidence: Regulated by the Pharmacy Board of Sierra Leone. Commercial licensing registries contain no valid active listings for therapeutic amphetamines or atomoxetine. Methylphenidate is tightly managed under hazardous drug laws to prevent abuse.
SL.notes: Clinical diagnostic frames for ADHD are extremely sparse. Travelers must declare medications clearly with verified stamps to avoid seizure.

SO.evidence: Regulated by the Somali National Medicines Regulatory Authority (NMRA). Modern central nervous system stimulants (amphetamines and methylphenidate) are not standardly registered, tracked, or distributed in the standard public healthcare sector.
SO.notes: Pharmaceutical pipelines lack standardized central tracking systems for psychotropics. Possession of highly active stimulants carries severe risk without exhaustive official diplomatic verification.

SS.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health. Due to extreme institutional challenges, national procurement does not accommodate modern ADHD psychopharmacology. Amphetamines are completely prohibited.
SS.notes: Supply chain is virtually non-existent for therapeutic stimulants. Bringing these compounds into transit zones without strict pre-clearance is highly discouraged.

TG.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie, du Médicament et des Laboratoires (DPML). Methylphenidate is cataloged under tight psychotropic controls in alignment with Francophone regulatory matrices. Amphetamines are strictly unapproved.
TG.notes: Stocks are limited and restricted to premier clinical networks in Lomé. Customs require official tracking certificates.

GH.evidence: Regulated by the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) of Ghana. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are registered on the national list of approved psychotropic substances under Act 851. Amphetamine formulations (like mixed amphetamine salts) are not routinely registered for commercial sale.
GH.notes: Classified as highly controlled psychotropic substances. Requires an official specialized prescription and a narcotics import authorization permit for travelers.

CM.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie, du Médicament et des Laboratoires (DPML). Methylphenidate is theoretically permitted for institutional psychiatric hospital use but is exceedingly difficult to source commercially. Amphetamines are not approved.
CM.notes: Severe localized availability bottlenecks. ADHD clinical support heavily relies on non-pharmacological or alternative sedative treatments due to lack of supply.

CI.evidence: Regulated by the Autorité Ivoirienne de Régulation Pharmaceutique (AIRP). Governed under strict French-inherited narcotic laws. Methylphenidate is accessible under rigorous psychotropic prescription, while amphetamines remain unregistered.
CI.notes: Requires a triplicate custom psychotropic prescription counter-signed by certified psychiatric experts in Abidjan.

SN.evidence: Regulated by the Agence Nationale de Régulation Pharmaceutique (ARP). Recently attained WHO Maturity Level 3. Methylphenidate is registered on the national psychotropic scheduled formulary under close monitoring. Amphetamines are completely unregistered.
SN.notes: Supply chain is strictly audited under the national pharmacy structure (PNA) to prevent illicit parallel trading.

MZ.evidence: Regulated by the National Directorate of Pharmacy (DNF). Central nervous system stimulants face heavily restricted clinical deployment. Methylphenidate is limited to dedicated provincial neuropsychiatric centers.
MZ.notes: Stocks are highly unreliable in public networks; private imports are subject to long regulatory delays and mandatory clinical justification.

AO.evidence: Regulated by the Agência Reguladora de Medicamentos e Tecnologias de Saúde (ARMED). Methylphenidate is registered under specialized narcotic controls. Amphetamines are strictly banned for therapeutic ADHD applications.
AO.notes: Travelers must hold legalized cross-border medical certificates in Portuguese to prevent seizure by customs authorities.

ZM.evidence: Regulated by the Zambia Medicines Regulatory Authority (ZAMRA). Methylphenidate is a registered Schedule 3 psychotropic drug. Atomoxetine is approved. Amphetamine salts are unlisted.
ZM.notes: Requires strict compliance with the Dangerous Drugs Act. Handled almost entirely through specialist private clinics or major tertiary institutions.

ZW.evidence: Regulated by the Medicines Control Authority of Zimbabwe (MCAZ). WHO Maturity Level 3 regulator. Methylphenidate is approved and monitored under the Dangerous Drugs Act. Amphetamines are strictly banned.
ZW.notes: Requires specialized pink narcotic prescription forms. Possession without authenticated tracking tags constitutes a severe felony.

BW.evidence: Regulated by the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA). Methylphenidate (5mg and 10mg) is integrated into the Botswana Essential Medicines List (BEML). Amphetamines are not standardly registered.
BW.notes: Requires specific psychiatric authorization (designated with 'E' class restrictions in national listings).

NA.evidence: Regulated by the Namibia Medicines Regulatory Council (NMRC). Methylphenidate is widely approved (e.g., Concerta, Ritalin formulations) under tight Schedule 5/6 classifications. Amphetamines are completely unregistered.
NA.notes: Strict cross-border control links with South African supply lines. Requires structured medical validation forms at point of entry.

MG.evidence: Regulated by the Agence de Médicament de Madagascar (DAMM). Severe structural shortage of psychiatric drugs. Methylphenidate is occasionally imported under exceptional authorizations; amphetamines are completely unauthorized.
MG.notes: Therapeutic access is largely non-existent for the general population outside localized humanitarian or elite private medical pipelines.

MU.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health and Wellness. Methylphenidate HCl 10mg tablets are integrated into the Approved Drug List for Public Hospitals. Governed under the Dangerous Drugs Act. Amphetamines are severely restricted.
MU.notes: Requires a specialized narcotic prescription form and official government-issued psychotropic authorization for travel import.

TN.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are reported to be available in Tunisia. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved. Limited regulatory information available.

KP.evidence: There is no formal national prevalence data or standardized psychiatric recognition for neurodevelopmental disorders like ADHD. Central nervous system stimulants like medical-grade methylphenidate or amphetamines are not officially registered, procured, or distributed within the public health infrastructure. Chronic medication shortages mean physical and communicable diseases are strictly prioritized.
KP.notes: Due to a lack of commercial healthcare pipelines, behavioral challenges are typically managed via domestic discipline or ideological training rather than evidence-based pharmacotherapy. Defector reports highlight severe local illicit markets for unprescribed methamphetamines used raw as homemade cure-alls, but legal, therapeutic ADHD stimulants do not exist. Any travel with psychotropic substances is opaque and carries a risk of harsh border interdiction without exhaustive diplomatic documentation.

MN.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health of Mongolia and the General Agency for Specialized Inspection. Methylphenidate is available strictly under tight psychotropic narcotic controls. Amphetamines are not registered for therapeutic use on the state medicine registry.
MN.notes: Stimulants are restricted to major psychiatric centers in Ulaanbaatar (such as the National Center for Mental Health). Travelers must carry an official doctor's note and declaration indicating personal medical use.

GL.evidence: Regulated by the Danish Medicines Agency (Lægemiddelstyrelsen) under Greenland's integrated healthcare agreement with Denmark. Methylphenidate and lisdexamfetamine are approved for ADHD treatment under strict prescription guidelines.
GL.notes: Follows Danish narcotic laws. Mixed amphetamine salts (Adderall) are not standardly approved. Travelers from Schengen countries require a Schengen medical certificate (Pillpas), while non-Schengen travelers require a comprehensive doctor's letter.

AQ.evidence: Antarctica has no central government, local population, or sovereign FDA. All medical rules are governed strictly by the national polar program of the country operating the specific research station (e.g., USAP for McMurdo Station, BAS for Rothera).
AQ.notes: Approval is programmatic rather than legislative. Station deployment requires a rigorous Physical Qualification (PQ) screening process. Certain ADHD stimulants require specialized medical waivers, comprehensive multi-month supply lines, and psychiatric clearance prior to deployment due to isolated winter-over conditions.

KZ.notes: Stimulant medications for ADHD, including methylphenidate and lisdexamfetamine, are generally not registered or are classified under extremely strict narcotic controls, making them effectively unavailable for standard clinical prescription. Atomoxetine is also rarely registered or accessible through local pharmacies. Patients often face significant legal and logistical barriers to obtaining these specific classes of medication.

KG.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are reported to be available in Kyrgyzstan. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved. Limited regulatory information available.

AM.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are reported to be available in Armenia. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved. Limited regulatory information available.

AZ.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are reported to be available in Azerbaijan. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved. Limited regulatory information available.

BG.evidence: Regulated by the Bulgarian Drug Agency (BDA) under the Ministry of Health and harmonized with the European Medicines Agency (EMA). Methylphenidate (primarily Concerta extended-release) and atomoxetine are registered on the official national pharmaceutical index. All amphetamine variants, including dexamphetamine and lisdexamfetamine, are completely unregistered and unavailable for therapeutic use.
BG.notes: Methylphenidate is available but requires strict narcotic prescription oversight. Amphetamine-based ADHD treatments are completely prohibited for domestic prescribing.

BY.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in Belarus. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved.

MD.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are reported to be available in Moldova. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved. Limited regulatory information available.

PE.notes: Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are available for ADHD treatment in Peru. Amphetamine-class stimulants are not approved.

VE.notes: Methylphenidate (e.g., Ritalin) is clinically approved and available, though supply is frequently subject to local market volatility and economic conditions. Lisdexamfetamine, amphetamine-based salts, and atomoxetine are generally not registered or are unavailable through official public clinical channels.

DZ.evidence: Regulated by the Ministère de la Santé and the National National Agency for Pharmaceutical Products (ANPP). Methylphenidate is approved but strictly classified as a Table A psychotropic substance. Amphetamines are not registered for therapeutic use.
DZ.notes: Prescriptions require specialized triplicate control forms issued exclusively by hospital psychiatrists. Strict quantity limits apply at customs.

BJ.evidence: Regulated by the Agence Béninoise de Régulation Pharmaceutique (ABRP). Follows rigid regional West African UEMOA narcotic guidelines. Methylphenidate is authorized under strict import quotas; amphetamines are completely unregistered.
BJ.notes: Sourcing is highly irregular and confined to select institutional pharmacies in Cotonou. Requires validated doctor authorization.

BF.evidence: Regulated by the Agence Nationale de Régulation Pharmaceutique (ANRP). Amphetamines are illegal for clinical medical use. Methylphenidate is legally classified under scheduled psychotropics but is rarely stocked in national distribution cycles.
BF.notes: Severe localized availability bottlenecks. Medical supplies face structural logistical disruptions outside major metropolitan centers.

BI.evidence: Regulated by the Autorité de Régulation des Médicaments et des Aliments (ABREMA). No registered commercial licenses exist for amphetamine salts, dexamphetamine, or lisdexamfetamine. Methylphenidate is theoretically classified as a controlled narcotic but lacks consistent formal import lines.
BI.notes: ADHD treatments are severely limited within the public system. Travelers face extreme scrutiny without legalized psychiatric documentation.

CF.evidence: Regulated by the Ministère de la Santé et de la Population. Central nervous system stimulants lack structured regulatory registry logs or standard tracking systems. Unauthorized amphetamines or methylphenidate are subject to immediate seizure.
CF.notes: Public healthcare infrastructure prioritizing endemic diseases; specialized neuropsychiatric medications are completely absent from normal commercial trade.

TD.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament. Commercial or therapeutic registration of amphetamine formulations is absent. Methylphenidate is heavily controlled and isolated strictly to military or direct ministry exceptions.
TD.notes: Strict border drug interdiction protocols are in effect. Possession without heavy official authorization is legally risky.

CG.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament (DPM) of the Republic of the Congo. Methylphenidate is approved strictly under custom import authorizations. Amphetamines are not registered for therapeutic distribution.
CG.notes: Highly scarce. Medications can generally only be sourced through highly specialized channels in Brazzaville or Pointe-Noire.

DJ.evidence: Regulated by the Ministère de la Santé. Methylphenidate is managed under tight narcotic scheduling rules matching historical French health frameworks. Amphetamines are not approved or imported.
DJ.notes: Stocks are rare and limited to specialized military or international private clinics in the capital city.

GQ.evidence: Regulated by the Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social. There is no public record of standard registrations for amphetamine products or atomoxetine. Methylphenidate is restricted under specific psychotropic monitoring laws.
GQ.notes: Relying on imported items with volatile stock rates. All personal quantities must be accompanied by certified Spanish translations of prescriptions.

ER.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health. Central nervous system stimulants (methylphenidate and amphetamines) are not listed on the national core formulary of essential medicines. Strictly restricted to avoid diversion.
ER.notes: Therapeutic infrastructure for neurodevelopmental care is severely underdeveloped. Bringing stimulants across checkpoints requires specialized state clearance.

SZ.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health. Closely follows South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) trends. Methylphenidate is registered as a Schedule 5/6 controlled substance. Amphetamines are not registered.
SZ.notes: Requires verified cross-border diagnostic forms. Sourced almost entirely from regional tertiary private medical networks.

GA.evidence: Regulated by the Agence du Médicament du Gabon (AMED). Methylphenidate is integrated into high-level psychotropic classifications. Amphetamine-based formulations are completely unregistered.
GA.notes: Requires mandatory validated documentation from a licensed psychiatric specialist to clear national custom entry ports.

GM.evidence: Regulated by the Medicines Control Agency (MCA) Gambia. Amphetamines are strictly unapproved. Methylphenidate is subject to high-level narcotic restrictions and is not routinely stocked in general public healthcare routes.
GM.notes: Requires direct individual clinical exception permits from the MCA for any legitimate personal transit imports.

GN.evidence: Regulated by the Direction Nationale de la Pharmacie et du Médicament (DNPM). Amphetamine formulations remain unregistered. Methylphenidate availability is unstable and strictly ring-fenced to specialized psychiatric programs.
GN.notes: High volumes of counterfeit products in parallel informal networks mean strict state checks are applied to genuine controlled prescriptions.

GW.evidence: Regulated by the Direcção-Geral da Farmácia. Formal public tracking or registration entries do not exist for modern ADHD stimulants. Amphetamines are strictly unapproved.
GW.notes: Severe systemic instability has limited access to psychiatric pharmaceuticals. Sourcing via public commercial channels is functionally non-existent.

LS.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health. Interlinked tightly with South African pharmaceutical regulatory listings. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are approved under controlled psychotropic classifications. Amphetamines are unregistered.
LS.notes: Dispensed almost exclusively at select specialized clinical points in Maseru. Border entry checks demand highly formalized medical tracking notes.

LR.evidence: Regulated by the Liberia Medicines and Health Products Regulatory Authority (LMHRA). Amphetamines are unlisted and prohibited. Methylphenidate is managed under dangerous psychotropic schedules with no stable retail tracking supply chain.
LR.notes: Access to pediatric or adult ADHD psychopharmacology is extremely constrained outside specialized international medical deployments.

MW.evidence: Regulated by the Pharmacy and Medicines Regulatory Authority (PMRA). Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are listed under strict narcotic and psychotropic schedules. Amphetamine configurations are not registered on the national database.
MW.notes: Requires custom certified pink prescription templates from psychiatric hospitals. Unauthorized imports are severely penalized under anti-diversion acts.

ML.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et du Médicament (DPM). Amphetamines are completely prohibited for therapeutic distribution. Methylphenidate is theoretically registered under restricted psychotropic guidelines.
ML.notes: Sourcing challenges are extreme. Supplies are rarely tracked outside specific institutional channels in Bamako.

MR.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et du Laboratoire. Psychotropic controls are exceptionally high to block illicit transit pipelines. Amphetamines are banned. Methylphenidate is heavily restricted and unavailable commercially.
MR.notes: Unverified stimulant medications found at security points carry a high risk of strict legal or border interdiction without exhaustive ministerial paperwork.

MA.evidence: Regulated by the Direction du Médicament et de la Pharmacie (DMP). Methylphenidate is fully approved and strictly cataloged under the 'Tableau A' narcotic designation. Atomoxetine is approved. Amphetamines are strictly unapproved.
MA.notes: Prescription renewals are strictly capped at limited-day cycles (typically 28 days) and require rigorous oversight from licensed neurologists or psychiatrists.

NE.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie et de la Médecine Traditionnelle. Therapeutic amphetamines are completely illegal. Methylphenidate is structurally controlled under psychotropic schedules with no routine domestic commercial distribution pipeline.
NE.notes: Severe systemic shortages disrupt mental health therapeutics. Carrying stimulants across internal security checkpoints is heavily restricted.

RW.evidence: Regulated by the Rwanda Food and Drugs Authority (Rwanda FDA). Achieved WHO Maturity Level 3. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are officially registered on the national list of approved human medicines. Amphetamines are not registered.
RW.notes: Strictly monitored as a controlled psychotropic substance. Dispensing requires validated tracking records from regional referral medical complexes.

SL.evidence: Regulated by the Pharmacy Board of Sierra Leone. Commercial licensing registries contain no valid active listings for therapeutic amphetamines or atomoxetine. Methylphenidate is tightly managed under hazardous drug laws to prevent abuse.
SL.notes: Clinical diagnostic frames for ADHD are extremely sparse. Travelers must declare medications clearly with verified stamps to avoid seizure.

SO.evidence: Regulated by the Somali National Medicines Regulatory Authority (NMRA). Modern central nervous system stimulants (amphetamines and methylphenidate) are not standardly registered, tracked, or distributed in the standard public healthcare sector.
SO.notes: Pharmaceutical pipelines lack standardized central tracking systems for psychotropics. Possession of highly active stimulants carries severe risk without exhaustive official diplomatic verification.

SS.evidence: Regulated by the Ministry of Health. Due to extreme institutional challenges, national procurement does not accommodate modern ADHD psychopharmacology. Amphetamines are completely prohibited.
SS.notes: Supply chain is virtually non-existent for therapeutic stimulants. Bringing these compounds into transit zones without strict pre-clearance is highly discouraged.

TG.evidence: Regulated by the Direction de la Pharmacie, du Médicament et des Laboratoires (DPML). Methylphenidate is cataloged under tight psychotropic controls in alignment with Francophone regulatory matrices. Amphetamines are strictly unapproved.
TG.notes: Stocks are limited and restricted to premier clinical networks in Lomé. Customs require official tracking certificates.
